title.title: BeaconMind
title.subtitle: A language model keeps its own pose and landmark map on a small robot car
lines: Xiaohui Chen
Replayed from the experiment's logs (simulation recorded {{sim.date-long}})
title.footer: Recorded demo: every number on screen is read from the project's log and evidence files by code.

idea.title: The model owns the map and the decisions; code does the geometry
lines: The car's camera sees AprilTags on the walls: the beacons. At every step the model gets the tag detections and the wheel odometry as text.
It calls geometry tools (odometry, association gate, position fix, map update), then writes a report: its pose, its beacon map and the next move.
A validator checks every move against the safety flags before anything is executed; a refused move executes nothing.
The mission shown here is EXPLORE: map as many beacons as possible, then stop.

sim_part.title: One closed-loop episode in a simulated copy of the real room
lines: kinsim, the kinematic simulator of the room: {{sim.tags}} AprilTags at their planned (nominal) positions, camera field of view {{cam.hfov}}°, range limit {{cl.range-m}} m.

Claude Opus 5.5 ({{cl.opus.model}}, effort {{cl.opus.effort}}) chose every move, live through the Anthropic API, on {{sim.date-long}}. Start pose {{sim.start}}; odometry noise seed {{sim.noise-seed}}.

!This video replays that run's logs: no model was called to make it. The simulator moves the car instantly; each move is drawn at its commanded speed ({{sim.v-max}} m/s, {{sim.w-max}}°/s). Thinking and driving are sped up, and both speeds are always shown.

sim_legend.title: What each part of the screen shows
lines: =1  The header: step, real time since the start, model cost so far, tags mapped, the believed pose's error, and the two speeds (thinking, driving); the one playing is filled.

=2  The room from above. Grey car, to scale: the simulator's true pose. Blue outline: the model's believed pose. Tags turn green once mapped; blue rings are the model's beacon estimates; yellow marks tags seen this step.
=3  A close-up that follows the car, and what its camera would see: the tags projected through the calibrated camera (amber: reported to the model).
=4  The step as the harness logged it: observation, tool calls and answers, the model's report, the validator's verdict.

lines: !One episode, one start pose, one noise seed: this shows the loop working, not that one method is better.
!Dead reckoning was more accurate here: the path is short and the simulated odometry drifts little.

validator.title: What a refused move looks like
lines: !This short clip is a scripted test model from the test suite, not a real model. The real episode above never needed a refusal ({{sim.refused}} refused moves).
The scripted model drives toward a wall in the study's {{rule.square-m}} m square, asks for moves the safety flags do not allow, then presses the emergency stop.
Same harness, same validator and the same move checks as the real episode ({{val.steps}} steps, {{val.refused}} moves refused, ended by {{val.ended-by}}).

car_part.title: The same harness on the real car
lines: Phone video, the car's own camera with the tags it detected, the room from above and the model's step trace, aligned on the Spark's clock.
!Waiting time is sped up; motion plays in real time. The speed is always shown.

closing.title: What the demo shows, and what it does not
lines: A language model ran the whole loop: it kept its own pose and beacon map, chose every move, and every move passed a validator first.
In this simulated episode it mapped {{cl.opus.tags-found}} of {{cl.n-tags}} tags with no phantom beacon and stopped by itself.

lines.text: Part 2 shows the same harness driving the real car.
